image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a grey whale surfacing in teal ocean water. The whale's head and anterior body are visible, showing characteristic mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches. A portion of a yellow and blue boat is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image angle is from the side/front, and the top of the head where blowholes are located is either submerged or obscured by the camera angle and water reflection. Cannot verify presence of two blowholes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white callosities/barnacle patches on the head and rostrum.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the head and shoulders; the posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior section is visible. While it looks robust, the full spindle shape cannot be verified as the tail is out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint; the visible skin texture matches the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are likely submerged or out of frame in this close-up of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution details show the rough, bumpy texture associated with cyamid infestations and barnacles.

artifact_observations.location: Water surface around the whale's snout
artifact_observations.reasoning: The foam and splash patterns near the snout appear slightly smudged and lack the crisp, chaotic detail of real water displacement, suggesting minor generative smoothing.
The yellow and blue object (likely a kayak or boat) has indistinct boundaries where it meets the water. The geometry seems to melt slightly into the waves rather than displacing them sharply.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a grey whale and not another cetacean species, given the specific skin patterns.
To rigorously assess the suspected melting artifacts at the boat-water boundary and the unnatural smoothness of the splash foam.
To check for edge bleeding between the whale's dark skin and the lighter water, ensuring the silhouette is physically coherent.

focus_areas: Water displacement physics around the snout
Geometric integrity of the boat hull
